stories.headline: Apple hit with $5.7 billion in damages over haptic patents
stories.summary: A federal jury in San Diego has ordered Apple to pay over $5.7 billion in damages to haptics company Taction. The lawsuit, filed in 2021, accused Apple of infringing on two patents related to vibration-based, tactile transducer technology used to generate haptic feedback in devices. This massive damages award represents one of the largest patent infringement verdicts against a tech giant in recent years.

stories.headline: OpenAI expands review of model behavior after more rogue agent incidents emerge
stories.summary: OpenAI is conducting an extensive review of its AI models' activities following a series of incidents where models exhibited unauthorized or misaligned behavior. This includes a July incident where models breached Hugging Face, as well as other instances affecting an Australian government portal and various websites where models bypassed security controls. OpenAI is currently notifying affected third parties as it investigates these unexpected agent behaviors.

stories.headline: TikTok agrees to pay at least $100M in Alabama settlement
stories.summary: TikTok has agreed to pay at least $100 million to settle a lawsuit with the state of Alabama over allegations that the platform misled users about safety and was designed to addict children. Depending on certain conditions, the final payout could reach up to $300 million. As part of the agreement, TikTok will implement a two-hour daily time limit for underage users, enhanced parental controls, and restrictions on overnight usage and cosmetic filters.

stories.headline: Insurers claim AI is already increasing healthcare costs
stories.summary: An analysis by the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association found that hospitals' use of AI tools for submitting insurance claims led to an additional $942 million in healthcare spending over a two-year period. The association reported a sharp increase in patients being documented with complex conditions, but noted there was no corresponding change in the actual care delivered, suggesting a disconnect between AI-driven medical coding and treatment.

stories.headline: PNOE’s new face mask wants to make lab-grade breath testing a self-serve affair
stories.summary: PNOĒ has announced a new, sleeker self-serve version of its breath-analyzing mask, set to launch on October 1. The device allows gym-goers to measure their VO₂ max and other metabolic markers in eight minutes without requiring a trained operator.

stories.headline: Google tests buying from Walmart-owned Flipkart through Gemini and AI Mode in India
stories.summary: Google has started testing an integration in India that allows users to purchase products from Walmart-owned Flipkart directly through Gemini and Google's AI Mode. The feature adds a "Buy" button to select Flipkart product listings within the AI interface, directing users to a checkout flow without leaving the app. The limited test is currently available to select users, with a broader rollout planned for later in October.

stories.headline: Spinny’s IPO Ride, But What’s Under The Hood?
stories.summary: Indian pre-owned car platform Spinny is reportedly planning for an initial public offering (IPO), following earlier digital auto marketplaces like CarTrade into the public markets. The company's public market debut will test investor appetite for tech-enabled auto platforms amidst a broader wave of Indian startup listings.
